A shared picture, different responsibilities

Useful for the rep.
Visible to the manager.

Explore the same process through three roles. These are practical examples of how people can use current records, not automated judgments about staff.

SALES MANAGER

What needs attention this Monday?

A proposal worth J$300,000 has had no activity in eight days. The account manager owns it, but the next action needs updating.

THE HUMAN NEXT STEP

Ask what changed, whether the buyer needs help and what date is realistic. Agree a specific next action rather than treating a stale record as a performance verdict.

Coach the process, with context.
Management and coaching

Review the work.
Improve the next conversation.

A useful pipeline review asks where decisions are slowing, whose workload needs support and what information is missing. Managers can coach qualification, proposal follow-through and handover using the context the team records.

Agree a daily action review and a regular management check-in. Coaching still depends on a conversation with the person, not simply a count of tasks or messages.

Stages & movement

Which opportunities progressed, stalled or slipped?

Ownership & workload

Is each active opportunity owned, with a realistic next action?

Customer understanding

Are decision-makers, requirements and open questions recorded?

Data quality

Are values, dates and outcomes current enough to trust?

From pipeline to planning

The forecast starts with the records.

Stage movement, opportunity value and expected timing feed reporting. Use them to examine current pipeline, expected revenue and opportunities needing attention, then discuss targets, staffing and purchasing with the assumptions visible.

Forecasting is an estimate, not guaranteed revenue or cash flow. Available reports and calculations depend on access, connected information and configuration.

Current customer & opportunity records↓Pipeline review & expected timing↓Management discussion & owned next actions

Cover without starting again

A colleague can read supported conversation history, notes and the next action before continuing an older quote. Relevant access permissions still apply.

Keep helpful automation connected

Configured reminders and assignments support a routine. Customer communication, AI assistance and workflow actions need agreed rules, permissions and boundaries.

Build a useful working habit

Keep records current, record outcomes honestly and review what the team uses. A CRM supports a good process; it does not create one on its own.

Keep the scope clear

Data cleanup, migration, custom fields, reporting and bespoke integrations need an agreed scope. No new setup or plan entitlements are promised here.
